questions.stem: On a velocity-time graph, a car accelerates uniformly from 0 to 30 m/s in 10 seconds, then travels at constant 30 m/s for 5 seconds. What is the total distance?
questions.explanation: Area = triangle + rectangle. Triangle: (1/2)(10)(30) = 150 m. Rectangle: 30 x 5 = 150 m. Total = 150 + 150 = 300 m.

questions.stem: To estimate the area under a curve, you can split it into strips. Using 4 strips of equal width under a curve from x = 0 to x = 8, each strip has width:
questions.explanation: Width = total range / number of strips = 8/4 = 2.

questions.stem: Using the trapezium rule with 3 strips to estimate the area under y = x^2 from x = 0 to x = 3, the strip width is 1. The y-values at x = 0, 1, 2, 3 are 0, 1, 4, 9. What is the estimate?
When the area under a velocity-time graph is below the time axis, this represents:

options.text: Distance travelled in the reverse direction

questions.explanation: Negative velocity means moving in the opposite direction. The area below the axis represents distance travelled in the reverse direction.

questions.stem: Using more strips (narrower trapeziums) in the trapezium rule generally makes the estimate:
questions.explanation: More strips means the straight-line tops of the trapeziums follow the curve more closely, giving a more accurate estimate of the actual area.
